notes.statement: Beijer et al. (2019) used next-generation sequencing to identify heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene in 3 unrelated families with autosomal dominant juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy. They noted variable penetrance in 2 of the 3 families, and disease severity varied greatly between patients.
quotes: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
Variable penetrance was noted for these mutations in two of three families, and phenotype severity differs greatly between patients.

notes.statement: Beijer et al. (2019) found that mutant SPTAN1 mRNA carrying the nonsense mutations was degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, which reduced alpha-II spectrin protein levels in patient cells. This pointed to haploinsufficiency, in contrast to the dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations previously reported in epilepsy phenotypes.
quotes: The mutant mRNA containing nonsense mutations is broken down by nonsense-mediated decay and leads to reduced protein levels in patient cells.
Previously, dominant-negative αII-spectrin gene mutations were described as causal in a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.

notes.statement: Beijer et al. (2019) described distal hereditary motor neuropathies as a rare subgroup of inherited peripheral neuropathies. They are marked by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant sensory involvement.
quotes: Distal hereditary motor neuropathies are a rare subgroup of inherited peripheral neuropathies hallmarked by a length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons.
